meta.description: All assumptions feeding the analytic Eco Chip energy/TOPS model.
meta.note: Every value here has a source (or 'derived') noted in ANALYTIC_ECOCHIP.md §Assumptions.

conventional_reactive_range.source: MLPerf inference results across data-center accelerators typically show sustained-vs-peak ratios in this band under continuous inference load; corroborated by NVIDIA's public MLPerf submissions where sustained throughput year-over-year gains of 60-150% relative to prior-year same-hardware imply substantial software-recoverable headroom above sustained hardware baseline

proactive_homeostatic_range.source: Apple M-series with aggressive DVFS sustains ~85-95% of peak on many workloads at lower TDPs (~20-40W); scaling to 460W stack with sufficient cooling budget puts achievable sustained fraction in the 70-88% range depending on cooling capacity

nvidia_h100_sxm5.source: NVIDIA H100 datasheet (peak); MLPerf inference v5.1 submissions (sustained observed)

nvidia_gh200_grace_hopper.note: Uses H100 GPU die; TOPS/W similar to H100 SXM5

cascade.source: BENCH_ECOCHIP.md v2 run: idle-delta measured energy per decision, B2 cascade vs B1 DistilBERT-alone
cascade.note: This ratio applies at software-decision level. It does NOT translate 1:1 into a hardware TOPS/W improvement — cascade reduces useful-decisions-per-cycle demand, not per-cycle efficiency. Reported here for decisions/J only, not TOPS/W.

die_area_and_power_density_estimates.compute_die_area_source: Comparable AI compute dies at 7nm range 600-1000 mm² (H100 GPU die is 814 mm² at TSMC 4N which is 7nm-class)
die_area_and_power_density_estimates.compute_die_power_density_source: Data-center AI accelerators sustain 5-10 W/mm² average heat flux with local hotspots higher; 0.19 W/mm² is well below thermal-density ceiling, consistent with a die designed for proactive homeostasis rather than peak-throttle operation
